findings.title: Installer trusts a predictable shared temporary parent
findings.attacker: Different local user able to precreate/control the selected tempdir/codex directory before installer use. Not a remote unauthenticated attacker.
findings.input: Directory ownership and replacement entries beneath an attacker-owned shared parent.
findings.flow: _tmp_root uses makedirs(exist_ok=True) without owner/mode/type verification; mkdtemp creates a private child; download/checkout, validation and copy later resolve child pathnames. Parent owner can rename child and replace it with a real directory containing different SKILL.md.
findings.impact: Integrity loss of newly installed skill instructions/helpers. Subsequent code execution or secret access is not demonstrated and requires later invocation/agent behavior.
findings.validation: installer_fixture.py ran actual main, validation and copying twice with mocked _prepare_repo and same-UID simulation of parent-owner replacement. Both installed AUDIT_REPLACEMENT_MARKER. No second-UID race, actual download, or active installation.
findings.counterevidence: mkdtemp gives random private child; installer rejects escapes and disallowed symlinks. These protect contents under a trusted parent, but not replacement by its owner. /tmp/codex was absent at observation; no compromise observed.
findings.recommendation: Supported upstream fix: verify owner-private real temp parent beneath trusted ancestors, or create private random staging directly beneath trusted temporary root; retain verified handles/identity across validation and copying. Pin immutable source revisions and recheck downloaded/copied integrity.
findings.reproduction: Run python3 evals/audit-2026-09-29/installer_fixture.py; writes only temporary fixtures.

findings.title: Managed manual helper exposes returned cache paths to parent-owner replacement
findings.attacker: Local user who precreates or controls selected shared cache directory, before use; no control of official HTTPS source assumed.
findings.input: Shared cache directory entries after content verification.
findings.flow: Default candidates include shared temp locations. stat/access establish writability, not ownership/privacy. Hash verification covers bytes read/fetched, then returns manualPath/outlinePath for a later consumer read. A controlling parent owner can replace those files after verification.
findings.impact: Documentation/outline integrity loss in subsequent reads. No credential disclosure or code execution established.
findings.validation: Current helper source reread; known mechanism remains. No direct helper invocation/import or shared-cache PoC because local instructions require the private wrapper exclusively. Safe reproduction specification: in a separate authorized harness, serve synthetic manual bytes and matching hash, use a controlled cache, replace returned file after verification and observe changed later read. NOT executed here.
findings.counterevidence: HEAD/body SHA256 prevents simple pre-fetch stale-content substitution. Private wrapper validates ancestors/owner/mode/non-symlink files and forces private cache; this mitigates the mandated workflow.
findings.recommendation: Keep invoking only the existing private wrapper. Request supported upstream owner/private-path checks and handle-bound consumption; do not patch .system.

findings.title: Security supplemental temporary artifact root lacks ownership verification
findings.attacker: Local user able to precreate predictable codex-security-artifacts-<hash> under shared process tmpdir. Must know/derive target context identity.
findings.input: Existing real directory and regular-file entries; symlink not needed.
findings.flow: storageContext derives predictable temp root, accepts EEXIST; root validation checks directory/symlink/canonical identity but not owner/private modes. sourcePath import reads a later regular file from that tree through native descriptors. A controlling parent can replace ordinary files before import.
findings.impact: Integrity of retained supplemental evidence. No canonical finding overwrite, confidentiality loss or code execution established.
findings.validation: Decoded current 49,554-line bundle as inert data and traced specific functions into native Python read guards. Did not fully audit bundle. No temporary MCP storage/sourcePath use or log/binary import performed. Safe reproduction specification: separate owner-private process test root, simulate precreated attacker-owned artifact root, replace regular evidence before persistent import, compare content. NOT executed here because actual plugin private temp runtime is unverified.
findings.counterevidence: Portable path and non-symlink descriptor checks prevent simple traversal/symlink escapes. Persistent inline storage bypasses vulnerable temporary import path and is mandatory locally.
findings.recommendation: Keep persistent inline supplemental artifacts. Verify an owner-private process-wide temporary parent before separately authorized restart and temporary use; request upstream owner/mode enforcement.
